feature: Debounce terminal output writes to reduce React re-renders
description: Terminal output from PTY processes can generate hundreds of write events per second during active builds. Each write triggers a React update cycle. Batching writes into animation frames would significantly reduce render overhead.

phases.description: Implement debounced terminal output writes using requestAnimationFrame

subtasks.title: Implement debounced write logic in useXterm hook
subtasks.description: Add requestAnimationFrame-based debouncing to batch multiple terminal output writes into a single xterm.write() call per animation frame. This will significantly reduce React update cycles during high-throughput terminal output (npm install, builds, test runs).
acceptance_criteria: Add a write buffer (ref) to accumulate incoming data chunks
Use requestAnimationFrame to schedule a flush of buffered data
Ensure only one animation frame is scheduled at a time
Flush buffered data to xterm.write() on each animation frame
Clear the buffer after flushing
Add cleanup logic to flush any pending data on unmount
Preserve existing write() and writeln() function signatures
Ensure no data loss during batching
subtasks.notes: The write() function at line 322-326 needs to be updated to buffer data and use requestAnimationFrame. The writeln() function should continue to work as before (immediate write with newline).

subtasks.title: Add unit tests for debounced write functionality
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive tests to verify that the debouncing logic correctly batches writes without losing data.
acceptance_criteria: Test that multiple rapid write() calls are batched into a single xterm.write()

technical_notes.architecture: The debouncing is implemented at the useXterm hook level, where the write() function interfaces with xterm.js. This is the optimal location because: (1) it's before the actual DOM manipulation by xterm.js, (2) it doesn't affect the PTY process or IPC communication, (3) it maintains separation of concerns.
technical_notes.performance: Using requestAnimationFrame ensures writes are synchronized with browser paint cycles, batching up to ~60 writes per second (at 60fps) instead of hundreds per second. This reduces React update overhead while maintaining smooth visual output.
technical_notes.data_flow: PTY process → pty-manager.ts (IPC send) → useTerminalEvents.ts (IPC receive + buffer manager) → Terminal.tsx (onOutput callback) → useXterm.ts write() [DEBOUNCE HERE] → xterm.js
edge_cases: Ensure buffer is flushed on unmount to prevent data loss
Handle rapid component mount/unmount cycles (React StrictMode)
Preserve writeln() immediate behavior for error messages
Consider impact on Claude session streaming output

data_loss.risk: Buffered data could be lost on component unmount
data_loss.mitigation: Add cleanup logic in dispose() to flush any pending buffered data before unmounting

delayed_output.risk: Users might perceive a delay in terminal output
delayed_output.mitigation: requestAnimationFrame runs at 60fps, so max delay is ~16ms which is imperceptible. If needed, add immediate flush for writeln() calls

test_complexity.risk: Testing async RAF behavior can be complex
test_complexity.mitigation: Use Jest's fake timers and RAF mocking. Follow existing test patterns in the codebase
